nodes.label: CONCEPTS.md — standing architectural intent
nodes.author: Luigi Marrandino
nodes.rationale: Holds standing invariants and their reasons so they survive the archiving of the open items that settled them.

nodes.label: D108: the estimator ships as chars-v2
nodes.norm_label: d108: the estimator ships as chars-v2
nodes.rationale: Prose measured 2.507 against a published 3.5, 28.4% away and outside D99's ±25% threshold. Under-counting prose by 40% means a believed 108000-token prompt is 151000, and it would ship silently because every trim assertion checks internal arithmetic a wrong constant satisfies. A new id because trim_record.estimator is what makes a stored record interpretable, which is false the moment one id has two arithmetics. Code moves with prose at 2.44 despite being inside the threshold, because one measured row and one guessed row is worse than either.

nodes.label: T69: the estimator differential
nodes.rationale: Reads all three input fields because reading input_tokens alone reports 2 (F-16's method note); asserts the two prose sizes agree within 2% so a broken baseline subtraction fails loudly rather than silently re-deriving a constant. Burns ~$1 against the maintainer's credential.

nodes.label: F-24: two agents in one crate are coupled by the crate, not by their file sets
nodes.community_name: T59: template.rs + estimate.rs — scanner and estimator
nodes.norm_label: f-24: two agents in one crate are coupled by the crate, not by their file sets
nodes.rationale: T59 and T61 touched disjoint files and still broke each other: model/skill.rs referenced a SkillBindingId model/ids.rs did not yet declare, so htui-core did not compile and T59's gates could not run. The file-set intersection test is necessary and not sufficient — the parallel unit is a crate that compiles, not a file nobody else opens.

nodes.label: F-28: a per-crate gate is not a gate
nodes.community_name: T59: template.rs + estimate.rs — scanner and estimator
nodes.norm_label: f-28: a per-crate gate is not a gate
nodes.rationale: T59 and T60 each reported green and each left a failure only the workspace suite sees, because their validation lines were -p scoped. Every remaining task's validation line is the workspace suite with --no-fail-fast, because cargo test otherwise stops at the first failing binary — how milestone 8 briefly called two broken suites green.

nodes.label: F-33: cargo doc --workspace is red at HEAD (CLEAN-1)
nodes.community_name: T59: template.rs + estimate.rs — scanner and estimator
nodes.norm_label: f-33: cargo doc --workspace is red at head (clean-1)
nodes.rationale: Fifteen errors confirmed by stashing, pre-existing before this milestone, so cargo doc --workspace cannot be a gate here; each task gates on cargo doc -p <its crates> --no-deps instead.

nodes.label: F-16 — §4.4's Claude constants are low by 28.4%
nodes.norm_label: f-16 — §4.4's claude constants are low by 28.4%
nodes.rationale: Assuming 3.5 chars/token where reality is 2.51 under-counts prose by 40%, and the 10% reserve exists to absorb a rounding error, not a 40% one; it would have shipped silently because every trim test asserts internal arithmetic only.

nodes.label: F-17 — the GPT/Gemini row is not measurable here
nodes.norm_label: f-17 — the gpt/gemini row is not measurable here
nodes.rationale: agy_acp_server emits no usage_update, so there is no per-turn token figure to difference; the row keeps ANA-5's values with the reason recorded rather than assumed.

nodes.label: F-18 — the conservative-default argument holds at 2.44
nodes.norm_label: f-18 — the conservative-default argument holds at 2.44
nodes.rationale: A lower chars-per-token yields a higher token estimate for the same text, so the measured row is genuinely the conservative default against both published rows — which it was not at 3.5.

nodes.label: Estimator probe method (all three input fields)
nodes.norm_label: estimator probe method (all three input fields)
nodes.rationale: input_tokens alone reports 2 because the CLI's system prompt lands in the cache fields — which is why the milestone-8 fixtures could not calibrate anything; corpora are in-tree and deterministic and the reply is pinned to one word so output tokens cannot move the input figure.

nodes.label: MOD-2 milestone 9 plan (prompt assembler + preview)
nodes.rationale: Structurally different from milestones 1–8: the assembler's production caller (graph run stage 3) is MOD-4's and does not exist, so a read-only preview is built as the only binary-level exercise, against the risk that the assembler ships correct but never executed and rots before MOD-4.

nodes.label: D109: preview refuses on Backend::Offline (PROMPT_ON_SERVER_ONLY)
nodes.rationale: An offline preview is not one missing setting but four unmirrored tables, so 'preview offline' meant a cache migration that renumbers MOD-4's a second time and rebuilds every box's mirror — cost for a feature the maintainer does not want. htui is an online-only program; refusing names the real reason in the one place a user meets it.

nodes.community_name: D110: no Repo fixture rows and no repos() read this milestone

nodes.label: F-29: MemStore::documents_of_kinds recursed forever
nodes.rationale: An empty kinds resolves to every kind the item has; for an item with no documents that is an empty kind list and the method re-enters itself. Presented as a stack-overflow SIGABRT, first misdiagnosed as async-future size. Fixed with an all.is_empty() guard.

nodes.label: F-30: §7.3 SQL had three defects, all found by running it
nodes.community_name: F-30: §7.3 SQL had three defects, all found by running it
nodes.norm_label: f-30: §7.3 sql had three defects, all found by running it
nodes.rationale: The ! nullability override is part of the output name Postgres sees so the bare alias does not exist; neither dialect clamped hops so hops==0 would return the whole depth-1 ring where MemStore returns nothing; SQLite has no DISTINCT ON and no array type so the mirror uses ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY kind) plus json_each.

nodes.community_name: F-31: H-29 overstated sqlx's nullability inference
nodes.norm_label: f-31: h-29 overstated sqlx's nullability inference
nodes.rationale: Measured rather than assumed: removing each override alone and recompiling against the live database shows only three are load-bearing, and all three are computed columns. The full set is kept for the links precedent, with the three that matter named in the method doc.

nodes.community_name: F-32: the two walks agree transitively through the shared spec
nodes.norm_label: f-32: the two walks agree transitively through the shared spec

nodes.label: MemStore over std::sync::RwLock<State>
nodes.rationale: Every trait body is one non-async closure with no .await at all, so holding a guard across a suspension point is structurally impossible; poison is recovered because State mutations are infallible map inserts and an unrelated panic must not take the store down.

nodes.label: Request seq, discriminant-keyed staleness and addressed replies
nodes.norm_label: request seq, discriminant-keyed staleness and addressed replies
nodes.rationale: Keying on the request discriminant rather than the id inside it is what makes fast selection movement correct — only the newest Item(_) reply per origin survives; replies are addressed rather than broadcast so no tab becomes a filter over another tab's data.

nodes.label: Store worker owns the Backend (D4)
nodes.rationale: No store handle exists on the render side, so R-NF-3 ("the UI never blocks") holds by construction rather than by convention; channels are unbounded because UnboundedSender::send takes &self and never awaits.

nodes.label: Workspace / project / repo hierarchy

nodes.label: No silent merges — divergence over last-writer-wins
nodes.norm_label: no silent merges — divergence over last-writer-wins

nodes.norm_label: one cache writer — the refresh task

nodes.rationale: SessionUpdate is a non_exhaustive tagged enum with no catch-all, so a typed decode of an unknown update is a serde error — and the claude adapter ships five such kinds. JSON in, DriverEvents out.

nodes.rationale: Update order within a turn is the SDK's ordered channel; a permission request is ordered only relative to events already forwarded and correlates by tool_call_id, never by seq adjacency.

nodes.rationale: The smallest resolver that starts the seeded claude row; stores nothing because the probe is milestone 5's.

nodes.label: D10: MSRV 1.98 and the new dependency set
nodes.norm_label: d10: msrv 1.98 and the new dependency set
nodes.rationale: Maintainer override of ANA-4 §4.2's 1.88: locked sqlx-core declares 1.94.0 and the toolchain is exact-pinned at 1.98.1, so 1.98 is the only number simultaneously true, checkable and equal to what CI runs.

nodes.label: D11: launch.rs types, ${tool} resolution, job-object spawn
nodes.norm_label: d11: launch.rs types, ${tool} resolution, job-object spawn
nodes.rationale: AcpAgentConfig's fields are private with a builder, so the SDK type is reached through the builder rather than by deserialising the row into it. No probe: ToolMap is an input; milestone 5's probe.rs fills it.

nodes.norm_label: d12: data-keyed driverfactory and adapter ids
nodes.rationale: R-AGT-5's 'a registry row and, at most, one stream adapter' is exactly one map entry per adapter and zero per agent; the fake reaching the factory through the same cli.stream knob a future adapter would use makes the proof structural rather than decorative.

nodes.rationale: The carry-forward is dropped because upsert_agent_box cannot write the two columns at all under D74; the old MOD-7 sentence is corrected rather than deleted so box registration does not rediscover the missing columns the hard way.

nodes.label: Recorder::latch_quota
nodes.rationale: Keeps last_quota_raw so a later row without a blob refreshes spend without erasing the windows (H-3); an Unreachable or NotFound backend disables the latch rather than failing the turn.

nodes.label: WriteStore::set_agent_box_quota
nodes.rationale: Every impl WriteStore must gain the method or nothing compiles, so the spies get delegating arms; rows_affected() == 0 is the NotFound.

nodes.label: htui-core store conformance CASES
nodes.rationale: Generic over WriteStore with no agent_box read, so 'probe byte-identical' is asserted where a read exists — mem.rs in-module and pg_criteria.rs with a raw SELECT.

nodes.label: WriteStore::upsert_agent_box
nodes.rationale: Under D74 it can neither set nor clear quota/quota_at — an AgentBox carrying them is not an error and not a write, the one sharp edge the design keeps and the conformance case pins.

nodes.label: UsageSpy
nodes.rationale: Delegates first and logs after, so no .await happens under the mutex guard.

nodes.label: D96: READ_CASES beside CASES, not a relaxed bound
nodes.norm_label: d96: read_cases beside cases, not a relaxed bound
nodes.rationale: run_case is already generic as run_case<S: WriteStore> and eleven of the 22 cases call write methods, so the bound cannot be relaxed without splitting every case; READ_CASES is additive so no existing case is touched, and CacheStore implements ReadStore only so CASES cannot exercise the mirror.

nodes.label: D67: set_agent_box_quota writes two columns only
nodes.norm_label: d67: set_agent_box_quota writes two columns only
nodes.rationale: Narrow on purpose: the latch runs inside a chat while a re-probe of the same row may run beside it, and two writers of one row must not be one statement wide. No insert, because a row never probed has no columns to latch into.

nodes.label: D74: single-writer quota columns
nodes.rationale: Carrying a quota value into an upsert statement that discards it was how a latch got lost; set_agent_box_quota becomes the only writer, and mem.rs must preserve the two columns on conflict or the conformance case passes on one backend and fails on the other.

nodes.label: BoundSkill::collapse
nodes.rationale: Kept pure in Rust and called by the SQL wrapper, MemStore and the assembler so every backend shares one override rule instead of reimplementing it in SQL.

nodes.label: BoxProfile::project
nodes.rationale: Drops BoxTool.path so no absolute path can reach digested text (H-1); tools sorted by name bytes and capped at 24.

nodes.label: Budget / target()
nodes.rationale: Reserve is held in basis points and target() is integer arithmetic, so no float rounding reaches the budget (H-9).

nodes.label: Inherent prompt reads (prompt_templates, bound_skills, box_profile, app_settings, repos, repo_paths, item_kind)
nodes.norm_label: inherent prompt reads (prompt_templates, bound_skills, box_profile, app_settings, repos, repo_paths, item_kind)

nodes.label: model::skill (Skill, SkillVersion, SkillBinding, BoundSkill)
nodes.rationale: SkillBindingId is its own newtype because skill_binding.id is a UUID primary key and the crate rule is one newtype per key.

nodes.label: tests/prompt_digest.rs
nodes.rationale: Carries no snapshots: structural asserts, so an insta corpus cannot hide a real change (H-11).

nodes.label: prompt::fixtures (test-support specs)
nodes.rationale: Every string a literal, no clock and no id, so a fixture spec digests identically on any box.

nodes.label: PromptSpec
nodes.rationale: Carries no RunId/StepId field so rule 8 (no run id, step id or absolute path in digested text) holds by type (H-2).

nodes.label: The nine ordering/determinism rules (§4.7)
nodes.rationale: Two boxes must agree on the digest whenever their inputs agree, so no clock, no absolute path, no id and no map iteration order may reach the rendered bytes.

nodes.label: BufferedWriter::set_step_prompt (offline refusal, E-8)
nodes.rationale: Refuses rather than no-ops: set_step_usage's no-op is licensed by upload_pending recomputing the figure from uploaded rows, but trim_record has no such source, and a silent no-op would leave a step with a prompt row and no audit — the one thing R-PRM-3 forbids.

nodes.label: prompt::digest (canonical, sha256_hex)
nodes.rationale: Uses the same sha2::Sha256 call record.rs:589 makes, so the recorder's recomputation is an identity and the two writers of prompt_digest agree by construction (H-7).

nodes.label: ExcerptProvider trait
nodes.rationale: Sync because a provider is a lookup by contract; the deadline runner gives it a thread instead of an async runtime.

nodes.label: htui-core prompt module surface (assemble)
nodes.rationale: assemble() takes the scrubber as an argument rather than a PromptSpec field because PromptSpec: Clone + PartialEq and dyn Scrubber is neither; purity by contract (invariant 2) means no store handle, no I/O, no clock, no map iteration reaches rendered bytes.

nodes.label: Recorder::record_prompt (unchanged, B.14)
nodes.rationale: No recorder change is needed: masking is idempotent and its Sha256 over the same bytes is identical to digest::sha256_hex, so D97's "assembler path passes None" is moot rather than unimplemented.

nodes.label: run_providers (deadline runner)
nodes.rationale: A provider that errors, panics or misses the deadline is dropped and recorded rather than failing the prompt; builtin is first and never dropped so a prompt always has a ranker.

nodes.label: WriteStore::set_step_prompt
nodes.rationale: Writes both prompt_digest and trim_record and nothing else — the pre-flight audit of R-PRM-3 written at stage 3 before a session starts; the same digest record_prompt recomputes, so the two writers agree by construction.

nodes.label: prompt::settings (budget chain, D101)
nodes.rationale: Defaults are compiled in and asserted equal to migration 0002's rows so the two cannot drift (H-30); budget_source is decided inside resolve_budget and nowhere else.

nodes.label: chat_live_agy.rs (T34)
nodes.rationale: Probe first then chat: only a written agent_box row makes the runtime spawn the recorded launch with --uid=; without it the chat resolves through tools::resolve and launches without the flag, the very H-3 defect.

nodes.rationale: Declarative credential tiers live in the registry row so no code path is keyed on an agent name (R-AGT-5); files are checked before env because on a subscription box the token file is the tier that fires (D63).

nodes.norm_label: d57: htui does not download the adapter

nodes.norm_label: d62: §11.14 answers as fixtures, mapper amended only if the wire demands

nodes.norm_label: d63: subscription oauth, not the api key

nodes.norm_label: d64: models filled from the live session/new answer or left empty

nodes.norm_label: t34 outstanding, blocked on maintainer oauth login

nodes.community_name: D79: a second registry row, claude-cli

nodes.community_name: D79: a second registry row, claude-cli
nodes.rationale: A spawn failure is a fact about the box's row, not the conversation: it is refreshed in the chat task's remaining life, off the worker's select! arm (R-NF-3).

nodes.community_name: D79: a second registry row, claude-cli

nodes.rationale: agent.transport is a property of a row and DriverFactory is keyed by transport; a row that silently changed transport mid-session would make DriverCaps a value that changes under the chat tab and MOD-4.

nodes.label: E-0: --bare never reads OAuth
nodes.community_name: D79: a second registry row, claude-cli
nodes.rationale: A row that is subscription + cli_rate_limit_event + --bare contradicts itself: under an API key there is no subscription allowance to latch.

nodes.label: pre-init buffer
nodes.community_name: D79: a second registry row, claude-cli
nodes.rationale: Without --bare, hook events precede system/init, so mapping them as they arrive would put an other row before the banner and fail session_banner_is_first_other_row on the live path only.

nodes.label: agent_claude_cli.json seed
nodes.community_name: D79: a second registry row, claude-cli
nodes.rationale: permission.default ask is inert on this row and kept only so the block parses identically to its siblings.

nodes.label: D79: a second registry row, claude-cli
nodes.community_name: D79: a second registry row, claude-cli
nodes.norm_label: d79: a second registry row, claude-cli
nodes.rationale: adapter_id_from and caps_from both branch on agent.transport, so one row cannot report two capability profiles; a dead settings.cli block on the acp row would leave two sources of truth for one dialect.

nodes.label: D92: --bare dropped from the seed
nodes.community_name: D79: a second registry row, claude-cli
nodes.rationale: --bare forces strictly ANTHROPIC_API_KEY auth, and subscription billing is the OAuth login, so a subscription row plus --bare contradicts itself and every live task would fail auth before reading a byte of stdin.

nodes.label: F-8: subtype success does not mean success
nodes.community_name: D79: a second registry row, claude-cli
nodes.norm_label: f-8: subtype success does not mean success
nodes.rationale: The terminal envelope is read through is_error and terminal_reason; subtype is a label, not a verdict.

nodes.label: H-4: unauthenticated snapshots are usable launches
nodes.norm_label: h-4: unauthenticated snapshots are usable launches
nodes.rationale: On Linux the recording is the only launch carrying --uid=, so a second resolution yields a dead adapter, not a worse message; unauthenticated certifies the binary is right and the box is not logged in.

nodes.label: launch_for
nodes.rationale: The disk check sits on the session's task because tools::resolve already puts its which and glob walks there, and a stale path must degrade into resolution on the same code path rather than fail a request on the loop.

nodes.label: D58: the driver prefers agent_box.probe.resolved
nodes.rationale: The recorded launch is by definition what AgentDriver::start spawns and is the only place the --uid= append exists; agy self-updates in place, so a recorded path can vanish and a chat must degrade to re-resolution rather than fail.

nodes.label: CliSession::answer_permission returns Unsupported
nodes.rationale: Transport would say the id is unknown while the truth is the operation does not exist on this transport, which is what Unsupported was added for; Closed comes first because a closed session should not claim to lack an operation it never had the chance to refuse.

nodes.label: Cancel drains before it synthesizes the done
nodes.norm_label: cancel drains before it synthesizes the done
nodes.rationale: Closes the milestone-3 defect class in both halves: a done written while lines are in flight, and an EOF taken as a clean end; the synthesized done is written only after the read side is exhausted or timed out.

nodes.label: cli/mod.rs supervisor
nodes.rationale: Shape copied from crate::acp — one task per session owning the child through a ChildGuard — with the difference stated once: no protocol layer, no permission channel, and cancellation is a signal rather than a notification.

nodes.label: stdin_line
nodes.rationale: The prompt always travels on stdin and never on argv, because a prompt on argv is visible in ps and the conformance harness has no argv to read (P-2).

nodes.label: D81: cancel is stdin-close then SIGINT then grace then kill
nodes.norm_label: d81: cancel is stdin-close then sigint then grace then kill
nodes.rationale: §4.4 leaves cancellation unverified with an explicit hypothesis; guessing would put an unverified claim in the one path criterion 5 measures, so T55 runs live before the code is written.

nodes.label: D84: system/init is the banner and the session id is htui's
nodes.norm_label: d84: system/init is the banner and the session id is htui's
nodes.rationale: session_banner_is_first_other_row is in CASES and adding a case is forbidden, so the CLI transport owes a banner; --session-id makes the id ours to mint rather than the agent's to report.

nodes.label: F-2: SIGINT yields aborted_streaming
nodes.rationale: The mapper keys done{cancelled} on terminal_reason == aborted_streaming rather than on the supervisor's memory of having sent the signal, and the cancelled turn reports no usage at all.

nodes.label: quota::available
nodes.rationale: spend and cap are the caller's run- or batch-level figures, not the blob's session spend: a session is not a run.

nodes.label: Plan: MOD-2 driver seam, registry and extensibility proof (M1-M2)
nodes.norm_label: plan: mod-2 driver seam, registry and extensibility proof (m1-m2)

nodes.norm_label: blueprint: mod-2 milestone 4 — durable history and replay

nodes.norm_label: d72: available() implements r-agt-8's four skip rules

nodes.rationale: A failed cancel is logged, not returned: the kill path already ended the session and the rows still have to be written.

nodes.rationale: Signature unchanged so 18 call sites do not move; the grace the cancel uses rides on RunCap instead.

nodes.label: Recorder::record_cap_breach
nodes.rationale: The transport's own done is withheld and re-synthesized because its stop_reason may be end_turn when the agent finished inside the grace window, and criterion 8 says the last row says cancelled; its scrubbed raw and at are kept so keep_raw_events still explains it.

nodes.rationale: It is pump's shape with one difference: the pull and the command channel have to be served by the same loop, which is why production never calls pump.

nodes.norm_label: production_half truncates in-module test blocks for the vendor sweep
nodes.rationale: agy_acp_server already appears in src/ seven times, every one inside a #[cfg(test)] mod tests block, and htui-core/src is off-limits to this item — so the offenders cannot be edited away. In-module tests are test code by the same rule that exempts tests/.

nodes.community_name: T4: the registry reader and the pre-flight
nodes.norm_label: p-9: a downgrade is refused at pre-flight as outranked
nodes.rationale: Installing a lower version beside a higher one would promote, watch the glob resolve the sibling, fail the post-promote check and roll back — a wasted download refused after the fact.

nodes.label: D12: Discovery.install as the declared source, InstallPlan as consent evidence
nodes.community_name: T4: the registry reader and the pre-flight
nodes.norm_label: d12: discovery.install as the declared source, installplan as consent evidence
nodes.rationale: The registry is mutable with no pinned snapshot URL, so the plan value is the consent evidence: what the user said yes to is what is installed, and InstallConfirm carries the plan back rather than re-reading a document that may have moved.

nodes.community_name: T4: the registry reader and the pre-flight
nodes.norm_label: d13: exactly one get and one head before consent
nodes.rationale: R-AGT-10's wording is 'told that before the download, not after': the HEAD transfers no adapter bytes, the body is the fetch. A second keystroke for the licence would be ceremony the PRD did not ask for.

nodes.norm_label: h-10: the single-install claim covers planning and installing
nodes.rationale: Two installs of the same id would race on .staging/, both promote, and one's retention would delete the other's version.

nodes.label: H-8: abort() does not stop spawn_blocking
nodes.community_name: D18: three install requests, one streamed reply
nodes.norm_label: h-8: abort() does not stop spawn_blocking
nodes.rationale: Shutdown during a 2 GB unpack would leave a thread writing into .staging/ after the runtime is gone; the unpack checks the token per entry and shutdown cancels before aborting.

nodes.label: D18: three install requests, one streamed reply
nodes.community_name: D18: three install requests, one streamed reply
nodes.norm_label: d18: three install requests, one streamed reply
nodes.rationale: The ProbeAgents shape enforces R-NF-3 by ownership: the Writer is taken before the spawn, the task owns it, the loop continues. Cooperative cancellation through a token rather than abort() so the task can sweep its staging entry and send the final frame. 250 ms matches the event loop's TICK, so a faster stream would only queue frames nobody sees.

nodes.label: D19: in-section consent pane with a row cursor, not an overlay
nodes.community_name: D18: three install requests, one streamed reply
nodes.norm_label: d19: in-section consent pane with a row cursor, not an overlay
nodes.rationale: The overlay factory is Fn() -> Box<dyn Overlay> with no argument, so an overlay cannot be told which row, and replies to a popped overlay are dropped — the progress stream could never be addressed to the view that asked. The section holds the cursor and outlives the whole install.

nodes.rationale: The assembler's production caller is MOD-4's, so the preview is the only binary-level exercise of it and must drive the real path rather than a demo shortcut (D102); inputs a graph run supplies and a preview cannot get declared stand-ins rather than silent zeros (D103). nodes.label: PromptTab (backlog detail sub-tab)
nodes.rationale: No store handle (R-NF-3): assembly happens off the UI task and arrives as a reply; nothing in the tab parses the prompt text.

nodes.label: PromptScope (D95)
nodes.rationale: A separate type rather than a change to Scope: Scope means "always one workspace" and has twenty-plus consumers, while the upstream walk must also bound to a single project.

nodes.label: RepoReader trait
nodes.rationale: Read-only by type (invariant 6): list and read and nothing else; an unreadable path is an error, never a panic.

nodes.label: excerpt::select (§4.5 steps 3–9)
nodes.rationale: Pure over its reader so FakeRepoReader touches no filesystem; rejects candidates with absolute paths and notes them, closing H-1.

nodes.label: excerpt::skip_by_path
nodes.rationale: The ranker applies the path skip rules itself rather than leaving them to FsRepoReader, or the denylist would pass on the filesystem and fail on the fake (H-22).

nodes.label: StoreRequest/StoreReply::PromptPreview
nodes.rationale: Freshness uses App::is_fresh's per-(origin, discriminant) rule so a burst of j presses drops every stale preview.

nodes.label: assemble() — the §4.7 pipeline
nodes.rationale: One entry point kept pure so the same PromptSpec and scrubber rules yield the same bytes on any box; each pipeline step lives in the module that owns it.

nodes.label: AssembledPrompt
nodes.rationale: sections is kept alongside trim so a reader need not open the record; payload_sections delegates to TrimRecord::section_entries so there is exactly one map (ANA-5 risk 12).

nodes.label: AssembleError
nodes.rationale: Unmasked names the section and the rule but never the text, so a scrub refusal cannot itself leak the residue.

nodes.label: run::prompt_summary (D106)
nodes.rationale: One derivation in one place so MemStore and the two SQL projections agree by test rather than by luck.

nodes.label: Runs pane prompt indicators (D106)
nodes.rationale: A second row line rather than a fifth column: the pane is 43 columns and the four existing columns plus spacing are 41, so ~120k ! would clip in any cell.

nodes.label: Per-section scrub (D100)
nodes.rationale: Each section's content is wrapped in Value::String, scrubbed, unwrapped — reusing the existing fail-closed Scrubber trait instead of a second scrub path, so the scrub runs before the digest (R-SEC-3).

nodes.label: SectionEntry
nodes.rationale: Constructed only by TrimRecord::section_entries; a grep asserts no other SectionEntry literal exists under crates/ outside trim.rs and its tests.

nodes.label: TrimRecord
nodes.rationale: to_value goes through BTreeMap so keys are byte-stable; section_entries is the single projection into the payload's sections[].

nodes.label: tests/estimator_live.rs (T69 probe)
nodes.rationale: Asserts the two prose sizes agree within 2% so a broken baseline subtraction fails loudly; #[ignore] because it calls a live CLI.

nodes.label: TokenEstimator (chars-v2)
nodes.rationale: Constants measured (D108) rather than published: 2.5 prose / 2.4 code against claude-opus-5[1m]; ANA-5's 3.5/3.0 was 28.4% off in the overflow direction, outside D99's ±25%. Two named ids (chars-v2 measured, chars-v1-gpt inherited) so trim_record.estimator says which arithmetic produced a record. Counts characters, not bytes, or CJK is 4× off (H-5).

nodes.label: TokenEstimator::estimate
nodes.rationale: Prose/code toggles are whole-line and exact so the estimate is a pure function of the bytes; the `<file ` toggle exists because the excerpt render is unfenced and would otherwise count as prose (H-23).

nodes.label: render::fence_for
nodes.rationale: Scans the whole content for the longest backtick run so nested fences cannot close early (H-4).

nodes.label: trim::head_tail
nodes.rationale: Binary-searches the largest surviving line count because the reclaim is monotone in k — ~12 estimates on a 4 000-line document instead of 4 000.

nodes.label: prompt::render — the section renderers
nodes.rationale: Renderers return content without the wrapper and wrap is applied once after trim, so every re-estimation includes the wrapper's own tokens; line endings are normalised on the way in (P-2) so every later byte count, marker and hash is over LF text.

nodes.label: SectionName
nodes.rationale: render() is one function with two uses (the name="…" attribute and the sections[].name key) so the two strings cannot drift; Box is a variant, never glob-imported, so it does not shadow Box<T> (H-24).

nodes.label: StepSummary::from_events
nodes.rationale: Deterministic summary of a step's own events built outside the assembler, so the assembler never sees an event.

nodes.label: prompt::trim — kept-first trim
nodes.rationale: Every strategy is written as change, re-wrap, re-estimate rather than arithmetic on the old count, because ANA-5 asks for re-estimation after every rung and only then are the marker's and wrapper's own tokens included. Section rows are created here and nowhere else (H-8).

nodes.label: trim::trim_order
nodes.rationale: Per-role orders follow §5.1's example over §4.4's row text (P-3); the document group sits before item and after verify_failure.

nodes.label: D86: usage sums modelUsage[*], not result.usage
nodes.norm_label: d86: usage sums modelusage[*], not result.usage
nodes.rationale: result.usage counts only the top-level loop and undercounts as soon as a subagent runs; the delta convention makes run_step.usage a plain sum, which is criterion 7.

nodes.label: F-13: normalize discards the CLI blob (measured)
nodes.norm_label: f-13: normalize discards the cli blob (measured)

nodes.norm_label: f-4: modelusage is cumulative, result.usage is per-turn
nodes.rationale: A mapper that summed modelUsage per result would double-count turn 1 into turn 2 and fail criterion 7 silently — the exact failure E-2 was raised to catch.

nodes.label: E-1: permission_answer is htui-authored only
nodes.rationale: Every row the recorder writes from a DriverEvent is stamped role agent while a policy answer must be role htui, so D85 as written is unreachable from a transport.

nodes.label: E-4: six cases need a second arm, not three
nodes.norm_label: e-4: six cases need a second arm, not three
nodes.rationale: The claude dialect carries cost on the terminal result only, so a harness cannot script a mid-turn usage without inventing a message the dialect does not have — the fabrication D80's own rationale forbids.

nodes.label: D80: capability-gated conformance case, not a skipped one
nodes.norm_label: d80: capability-gated conformance case, not a skipped one
nodes.rationale: Criterion 1 is 'adding a transport adds no case', not 'every transport can do everything'; a skip satisfies the letter and drops the coverage, and a harness fabricating permission requests would prove the harness, not the transport.

nodes.label: D85: permission_answer rows synthesized with by policy
nodes.norm_label: d85: permission_answer rows synthesized with by policy
nodes.rationale: The row is what makes a denial visible in the transcript at all, and marking it policy keeps it distinguishable from a user's answer.

nodes.label: D91: DriverCaps gains usage_mid_turn
nodes.rationale: Over the claude dialect cost is reported once at the end, so the cap-breach case's premise is not merely unmet but meaningless; naming the capability splits the contract instead of letting a transport quietly pass a case it cannot honour.

nodes.label: D93: permission_answer gets a twelfth DriverEvent variant
nodes.norm_label: d93: permission_answer gets a twelfth driverevent variant
nodes.rationale: A typed event makes the denial visible to the chat tab and to replay without a string comparison on an update field; the surviving boundary is the schema, since a kind outside chk_event_kind would need a migration.

nodes.label: D94: replay decodes permission_answer to the typed variant
nodes.norm_label: d94: replay decodes permission_answer to the typed variant
nodes.rationale: D93 left permission_answer with two shapes depending on direction — typed live, other on replay — so the chat tab would have read one kind two ways forever; serde(default) on denied is the honest reading for rows written before this milestone.

nodes.label: F-12b: permission denial has two sources
nodes.norm_label: f-12b: permission denial has two sources
nodes.rationale: The mapper takes the live system/permission_denied envelope so the refusal is recorded where it occurred, and suppresses the end-of-turn repeat by tool_use_id; one refusal is one row.

nodes.label: QuotaLatch
nodes.rationale: Carries source and billing as row-side facts — agent.settings.quota.source and agent.billing — never the agent's name (R-AGT-5).

nodes.label: Recorder
nodes.rationale: Holds no session and must not: it is what the conformance suite drives with no transport, so the cancel lives in the layer holding the session.

nodes.label: agent_worker::run_chat
nodes.rationale: On CapExceeded the run is Failed with stop reason Cancelled; the error row reaches the tab through the recorder's channel rather than a new DriverEvent variant (D73).

nodes.label: RunCap
nodes.rationale: The grace rides here so pump keeps its signature: the worker passes its CANCEL_GRACE, the conformance suite zero.

nodes.label: D97: set_step_usage keeps its third parameter
nodes.norm_label: d97: set_step_usage keeps its third parameter
nodes.rationale: Its only production caller is the free-standing chat path (record.rs:1072), whose digest is computed at record.rs:589 and which ANA-5 §4.1 puts outside the assembler's scope; traits.rs:86-91 already says the parameter survives this milestone.

nodes.label: D68: the latch never fails the turn
nodes.norm_label: d68: the latch never fails the turn
nodes.rationale: A buffered writer refuses registry writes with REGISTRY_ON_SERVER_ONLY, so the decision is made at start() rather than discovered on the first usage row: the usage rows are buffered and re-derive the figure after upload, and the last server-side value stands meanwhile.

nodes.label: H-1: the rustls provider must be installed explicitly
nodes.norm_label: h-1: the rustls provider must be installed explicitly
nodes.rationale: Client::builder().build() panics with 'No rustls crypto provider is configured' the first time i is pressed in production; a test in the suite makes that a red test rather than a field failure.

nodes.label: D22: documentation replacement and amendment records
nodes.norm_label: d22: documentation replacement and amendment records
nodes.rationale: The README section and the test constant are the third and fourth copies of a coordinate that goes stale silently. Old plans are history and stay as written; the phase note is where the tree says what changed.

nodes.label: D8: no new crate — the installer is htui_agent::install
nodes.norm_label: d8: no new crate — the installer is htui_agent::install
nodes.rationale: An installer is a producer for the probe's glob: it needs ProbeEnv, the expander, resolve_tool and probe_agent, all of which are probe.rs's. A separate crate would depend on htui-agent for every one and exist only to keep reqwest out of a manifest.

nodes.label: D9: reqwest 0.13 with rustls-no-provider, explicit provider install
nodes.norm_label: d9: reqwest 0.13 with rustls-no-provider, explicit provider install
nodes.rationale: D1 names progress bytes and cancellation as what a shell-out cannot give, and they decide the client: reqwest is async on the runtime the task already lives on, while ureq is blocking and a stalled server would hold a thread for tens of minutes — the hang D1 exists to avoid. rustls-no-provider keeps one crypto provider in the process, but the provider must be installed explicitly because reqwest does not infer the single enabled feature.

nodes.label: MOD-20 Registry-Driven Adapter Install Plan
nodes.rationale: All four milestones are planned as one dependency chain because milestones 1–2 are pure htui-agent work that milestone 3 consumes whole; splitting would only move the same task table across two files.

nodes.label: H-11: HTUI_TOOL_<NAME> precedence survives an install
nodes.norm_label: h-11: htui_tool_<name> precedence survives an install
nodes.rationale: The post-promote check uses resolve_tool without the override on purpose — it asks whether the glob sees the file, not what the box will run.

nodes.label: H-3: staging must stay outside the glob's reach
nodes.norm_label: h-3: staging must stay outside the glob's reach
nodes.rationale: A half-unpacked tree that resolves would spawn and die, breaking R-AGT-6 at the source.

nodes.label: H-4: the post-promote resolve check
nodes.rationale: Without it the installer could write where the seed does not look and the row would still say missing with a 2 GB tree on disk; this is the D5 agreement enforced at run time.

nodes.label: P-10: set-aside entries carry a .previous suffix
nodes.norm_label: p-10: set-aside entries carry a .previous suffix
nodes.rationale: A task aborted between the set-aside move and the restore would leave the working version in .staging/ for the sweep to delete — D3's 'a failed install never costs the working one' broken by the sweep itself.

nodes.label: D16: staging, promotion, rollback, retention
nodes.rationale: .staging/ is a sibling of <id>/ and the seed pattern's literal root ends at <id>, so nothing in staging can ever be walked — the 'interrupted install leaves nothing the glob resolves' metric holds by directory layout. Case (c) exists because rolling back a 682 MB download for a PATH problem would punish the wrong thing.

nodes.label: T6: the pipeline — re-probe, rollback, retention, cancellation
nodes.norm_label: t6: the pipeline — re-probe, rollback, retention, cancellation

nodes.label: T9: amp-acp live, the R-AGT-5 proof
nodes.norm_label: t9: amp-acp live, the r-agt-5 proof
nodes.rationale: Different vendor, .tar.gz, a published digest, Apache-2.0 — installed live from a registry row the test file itself writes, so nothing is keyed on an agent's name.

nodes.label: The fixture upstream diamond (C.4)
nodes.rationale: Only origin edges and a blocked_by to a done item are added, so no pinned set (links_hops_1_vs_2, the ready list, the tombstone case, the Graph snapshot) moves (H-14).

nodes.label: MemStore upstream walk (C.3)
nodes.rationale: Follows to_item_id only — directed, unlike link_graph; a seen set gives MIN(depth) for free.

nodes.label: Postgres upstream CTE (C.1)
nodes.rationale: The !/? overrides are required because query_as! infers every recursive-CTE column nullable (H-29); the $3::uuid cast is what lets query! type a nullable workspace parameter.

nodes.label: READ_CASES (D96)
nodes.rationale: Read-only and additive so the mirror can be a conformance target too; names only ReadStore methods, never an inherent (H-25).

nodes.label: ReadStore additions (document, documents_of_kinds, upstream_summaries, project)
nodes.rationale: These four sit on ReadStore rather than as inherents because their data is mirrored, which is what lets the mirror be a READ_CASES target (D96).

nodes.label: SQLite mirror upstream CTE (C.2)
nodes.rationale: No LATERAL, so a correlated subquery; plain ? placeholders bound positionally per the file's own style, which is why the workspace is bound twice rather than using ?NNN.

nodes.label: UpstreamEntry + sort_canonical
nodes.rationale: Sorted in Rust after every backend's own ORDER BY because Postgres orders qualified_key by collation and the mirror by bytes; str::cmp is byte order, so one sort reconciles all three.

nodes.label: P-1: pump is not the production loop, run_turn is
nodes.norm_label: p-1: pump is not the production loop, run_turn is
nodes.rationale: pump is what the conformance suites drive; production's run_chat drives run_turn, so the cancel-and-close sequence is one shared enforce_breach called from both.

nodes.label: D69: detection in the recorder, cancellation in the loop holding the session
nodes.norm_label: d69: detection in the recorder, cancellation in the loop holding the session
nodes.rationale: ANA-4 §7's claim that the recorder calls AgentSession::cancel() is not implementable: Recorder has no session field, and giving it one would put the transport back inside a recorder milestone 1 deliberately kept transport-neutral. Detection is the reason §7 names the recorder, and detection is what stays.

nodes.label: D70: caps read from project.settings via inherent project_settings, no migration
nodes.norm_label: d70: caps read from project.settings via inherent project_settings, no migration
nodes.rationale: The keys are already documented project.settings JSON and MOD-4 reserved 0003_orchestration.sql, so a migration would collide or be a fourth forward-only file for data needing no DDL. Micros because a float cap compared against an integer running total is a rounding argument waiting to happen.

nodes.label: D75: edit_proposal dedup index becomes step-scoped
nodes.norm_label: d75: edit_proposal dedup index becomes step-scoped
nodes.rationale: Criterion 6 currently passes only against the fake, which never flushes mid-call. The index must survive a flush because a flush is a persistence detail and (tool_call_id, path) identity is a domain fact.

nodes.label: D77: reserve the seq at announcement, defer only the write
nodes.norm_label: d77: reserve the seq at announcement, defer only the write
nodes.rationale: Persistence and display are already separate — the recorder sends its UI frame at announcement and only the database write waits — so nothing the user sees moves and replay reads by seq. The price is one crash window, accepted knowingly.

nodes.label: T46: criterion 6's dedup survives a flush
nodes.norm_label: t46: criterion 6's dedup survives a flush

nodes.label: agy_live.rs (T33)
nodes.rationale: Preconditions are stated so a miss is loud and named; the box's credential state is observed, not assumed, and session/new is driven so the model list costs no tokens.

nodes.label: CredentialTier
nodes.rationale: Records which tier answered and never the value, so a token's contents cannot leak into a log or a stored snapshot; the file tier is a stat.

nodes.label: probe_agent ordered steps
nodes.rationale: The credential check runs at step 2, right after agent.launch parses and before probe_tools, so every snapshot with a parsed launch records a tier — a missing box still says whether it holds a token.

nodes.label: ProbeSnapshot
nodes.rationale: The new credential key is #[serde(default)] so a pre-milestone-6 row still parses as None, which is the rule that row was written under.

nodes.label: resolve_credential
nodes.rationale: Files are walked through glob_first so the expander grammar, the spawn_blocking walk and the unset-variable skip rule stay the walker's own; a transport fault must not read as 'no credential'.

nodes.label: status_for
nodes.rationale: An empty auth_methods is ready whatever credential says, so claude's adapter is unaffected by D59; a row declaring no credential block keeps milestone 5's rule verbatim.

nodes.label: cli/claude.rs mapper
nodes.rationale: JSON read by key, never a typed decode, so a vendor shape the mapper does not know lands in other verbatim instead of breaking the build.

nodes.label: H-8: partial messages deliver text twice
nodes.norm_label: h-8: partial messages deliver text twice
nodes.rationale: --include-partial-messages delivers text as deltas and again inside the full assistant message; a streamed set keyed on the message id dedupes while a message with no deltas still maps from the full message.

nodes.label: D82: thinking blocks probed then mapped
nodes.norm_label: d82: thinking blocks probed then mapped
nodes.rationale: Thinking was off in the runs captured when ANA-4 was written, so the shape is unverifiable from a document and the fixture wins over §6.2.

nodes.label: F-6: thinking is signalled but not disclosed
nodes.norm_label: f-6: thinking is signalled but not disclosed
nodes.rationale: signature_delta is a cryptographic block signature, not words, so it is never appended to thought text; an empty thought stays empty rather than being invented or dropped.

nodes.label: F-7: coalescing key is (message.id, block index)
nodes.norm_label: f-7: coalescing key is (message.id, block index)
nodes.rationale: The thinking envelope and the text envelope share one message.id, so coalescing on the id alone would fold the thought and the reply into one event.

nodes.label: Fixture redaction holes: split deltas and slugged paths
nodes.norm_label: fixture redaction holes: split deltas and slugged paths
nodes.rationale: A needle only has to arrive spelled another way to walk through the rule; both holes were found by a later case reading an earlier case's committed fixture, which argues for keeping fixtures under test rather than merely under version control.

nodes.label: CapError
nodes.rationale: Plain struct with a hand-written Display, as model::ParseEnumError, because htui-core's one thiserror type is StoreError.

nodes.label: project_settings(ProjectId)
nodes.rationale: Inherent for the reason agents() is — Backend dispatches, no trait method — and the mirror carries the column, so every backend answers.

nodes.label: ProjectCaps
nodes.rationale: Anything that is not a non-negative integer errors rather than being ignored, because a cap the operator wrote and htui ignored is 'wrong by a factor of a million' in the other direction; 0 is a real cap that cancels on the first row reporting any USD cost.

nodes.label: agent_worker::start
nodes.rationale: The caps read joins box_info, this_user and agents() on the worker's task because the chat task does not yet exist and run_chat holds a Writer, not the Backend.

nodes.label: D70: per-run cap enforced by the recorder, in USD micros
nodes.norm_label: d70: per-run cap enforced by the recorder, in usd micros
nodes.rationale: The caps are read once at ChatStart on the worker's task beside the three existing registry reads, off the UI task by the same argument (R-NF-3), because run_chat holds a Writer rather than the Backend that dispatches project_settings.

nodes.label: D71: the batch cap is read and reported, not enforced here
nodes.norm_label: d71: the batch cap is read and reported, not enforced here
nodes.rationale: Enforcement is MOD-12's per ANA-4:1283; a chat logs that the key is set and does not act on it.

nodes.label: D17: the consent record is manifest.json on the box's disk
nodes.community_name: D17: the consent record is manifest.json on the box's disk
nodes.norm_label: d17: the consent record is manifest.json on the box's disk
nodes.rationale: Consent is a fact about this box and the strongest box-local home is the box's own disk. agent_box needs a column, therefore a migration, therefore MOD-4's promised 0003; box.settings is MOD-7's seam; app_setting is global; box.toml is htui-store's and the installer is htui-agent's. One manifest per id because version directories are deleted and the digest must outlive them.

nodes.label: H-6: the latch firing on a row re-probed mid-session
nodes.community_name: D17: the consent record is manifest.json on the box's disk
nodes.norm_label: h-6: the latch firing on a row re-probed mid-session
nodes.rationale: run_reprobe writes the whole row through upsert_agent_box carrying the quota it read at start(), so every latch between the re-probe's read and its write is discarded — a lost update by construction, not a timing accident.

nodes.label: D67: the narrow WriteStore::set_agent_box_quota setter
nodes.community_name: D17: the consent record is manifest.json on the box's disk
nodes.rationale: upsert_agent_box writes probe too, so latching through it would clobber the probe snapshot or force the writer to carry a full row it never read; two writers of one row must not be one statement wide.

nodes.label: D74: quota columns become single-writer
nodes.community_name: D17: the consent record is manifest.json on the box's disk
nodes.rationale: The probe reads existing at chat start and writes it back seconds later, discarding every latch in between — a lost update by construction. Making the column single-writer is cheaper than making two writers agree and is enforced by the schema access pattern rather than by a comment.

nodes.label: T38: the narrow quota setter
nodes.community_name: D17: the consent record is manifest.json on the box's disk

nodes.label: T45: single-writer quota columns
nodes.community_name: D17: the consent record is manifest.json on the box's disk
nodes.rationale: Serial after T38 because it touches the same four store files and T38's set_agent_box_quota has to exist before anything can prove it is the only writer.

nodes.label: ChildGuard behind a Mutex, swapped out before the await (D61)
nodes.community_name: MOD-2 milestone 6 blueprint — agy over ACP
nodes.norm_label: childguard behind a mutex, swapped out before the await (d61)
nodes.rationale: kill_and_reap is an async fn(&mut self) that cannot be awaited under the Mutex, so the guard is replaced under the lock and awaited on the taken value; awaiting the aborted task makes the Err mean "the kill has been sent" rather than "will be sent shortly", which is how open_session's timeout stops orphaning its adapter.

nodes.label: AcpDriver::launch_for — spawn the probe's recorded launch
nodes.community_name: MOD-2 milestone 6 blueprint — agy over ACP
nodes.norm_label: acpdriver::launch_for — spawn the probe's recorded launch
nodes.rationale: D58: the driver spawns agent_box.probe.resolved rather than resolving a second time, because that is the only path carrying a glob tool's per-platform args — without the mandatory --uid= the agy server aborts in ChangeRootAndUser before reading stdin. spec.env is applied last and wins, since the row's environment holds paths and the spec's holds secrets (R-SEC-2).

nodes.label: ProbeSnapshot::recorded_launch — D58's three row-side rules
nodes.community_name: MOD-2 milestone 6 blueprint — agy over ACP
nodes.rationale: A manual row is a human's path that launch::resolve already honours; ready and unauthenticated recorded the right launch (the vendor's auth error is more use than a second resolution) while missing has nothing to spawn and failed recorded a launch that did not answer. The fourth rule — the command still exists — is I/O and belongs to the caller.

nodes.label: Re-probe on a failed spawn, inline in run_chat (D60)
nodes.community_name: MOD-2 milestone 6 blueprint — agy over ACP
nodes.norm_label: re-probe on a failed spawn, inline in run_chat (d60)
nodes.rationale: The failure surfaces inside run_chat, a task with no handle to AgentRuntime.background, so ReprobeArgs travels in ChatArgs and the re-probe is awaited after the failure frame — off the worker arm by construction and deterministic in the harness. A runtime-wide claim stops two chats probing one row; there is no transport fallback, because a CLI agent is its own registry row.

nodes.label: SessionOptions.handshake_timeout injected per session
nodes.community_name: MOD-2 milestone 6 blueprint — agy over ACP
nodes.rationale: HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT is a const and stays the documented default; a test proving the timeout arm kills its child sets milliseconds instead of waiting a minute, and needs no test-support gate because open_session and AcpIo are already public.

nodes.label: MOD-2 milestone 6 blueprint — agy over ACP
nodes.community_name: MOD-2 milestone 6 blueprint — agy over ACP
nodes.norm_label: mod-2 milestone 6 blueprint — agy over acp
nodes.rationale: Where the plan and the tree disagree the tree wins and the point is marked plan ≠ tree; unverified claims are marked for the implementer to check.

nodes.label: prompt::defaults (DEFAULT_TEMPLATES, COMMAND_QUEUE_TEXT)
nodes.rationale: Bodies are string literals rather than include_str! so cargo doc shows them; COMMAND_QUEUE_TEXT is fixed in code because every byte of a section is a digest input.

nodes.label: prompt::template — the {{name}} scanner
nodes.rationale: One spelling per body: the four ANA-5 checks fall out of a single char_indices walk, and a placeholder must terminate before the next newline so an unterminated brace fails loudly.

nodes.label: TemplateRole (Phase, Judge, Handoff)
nodes.rationale: judge and handoff are reserved names, so role is derived from the template name rather than stored twice.

nodes.label: H-2: Response::content_length() lies on a HEAD
nodes.community_name: T5: fetch, verify, unpack, promote, manifest
nodes.norm_label: h-2: response::content_length() lies on a head
nodes.rationale: On a HEAD it reports the empty body's 0, so every plan would say '0 bytes', the D11 check would never refuse and the consent text would lie.

nodes.label: H-5: the executable bit versus launch::spawn's which
nodes.community_name: T5: fetch, verify, unpack, promote, manifest
nodes.norm_label: h-5: the executable bit versus launch::spawn's which
nodes.rationale: which::which refuses a 0644 file even on an absolute path, so a tarball with plain modes would probe failed; setting the bit in staging before promote means the promoted tree is never non-executable for an instant.

nodes.label: D10: zip deflate-only, tar, flate2; download then unpack
nodes.community_name: T5: fetch, verify, unpack, promote, manifest
nodes.norm_label: d10: zip deflate-only, tar, flate2; download then unpack
nodes.rationale: The two real archives are deflate and gzip, so enabling deflate64/bzip2/zstd/lzma buys decompressors nobody has an archive for. Download-then-unpack because a zip's directory is at its end and the digest must be checked over the whole file before a byte is unpacked.

nodes.label: D11: free space via fs4, refuse below 4× content-length
nodes.community_name: T5: fetch, verify, unpack, promote, manifest
nodes.norm_label: d11: free space via fs4, refuse below 4× content-length
nodes.rationale: The factor comes from measurement: a 682 MB archive unpacks to 2.0 GB (2.95×) plus the archive on disk during the unpack (3.95×), rounded up. The size is read from the content-length header because on a HEAD reqwest reports the body length, Some(0).

nodes.label: T5: fetch, verify, unpack, promote, manifest
nodes.community_name: T5: fetch, verify, unpack, promote, manifest

nodes.norm_label: snapshot files are part of a task's file set

nodes.label: D65: T34 runs first, its answers are inputs
nodes.norm_label: d65: t34 runs first, its answers are inputs
nodes.rationale: ANA-4 §7 marks the agy row 'Unverified'; writing the latch first and then discovering the shape is the failure mode the live-probe discipline exists to prevent — milestone 6 already paid for guessing once.

nodes.norm_label: t34: a live agy chat through the production runtime

nodes.rationale: Already the probe's answer to the same failure, so the session task adopts it instead of inventing a second ownership shape.

nodes.label: H-1: tokio orphan queue reaps the signalled child
nodes.norm_label: h-1: tokio orphan queue reaps the signalled child
nodes.rationale: Dropping an unwaited Child pushes it onto tokio's global orphan queue, drained on every park once SIGCHLD arrives; a reaper task would duplicate the runtime, so the idea is withdrawn.

nodes.label: open_session handshake timeout
nodes.rationale: Aborting the task drops the ChildGuard, whose Drop signals the kill; waiting for the task instead would turn a hung adapter into a 120-second chat start rather than 60 (D61).

nodes.label: D61: session task's child moves into a ChildGuard
nodes.norm_label: d61: session task's child moves into a childguard
nodes.rationale: The guard already exists and is the probe's answer to the same failure; teaching open_session to wait would double the worst-case chat start.

nodes.label: argv
nodes.rationale: extra_args go last so an operator's flag wins a repeated one; exactly one of --session-id and --resume is passed because the CLI refuses both.

nodes.label: D83: --max-budget-usd carries the per-run cap as a second cap
nodes.norm_label: d83: --max-budget-usd carries the per-run cap as a second cap
nodes.rationale: A server-side cap exists beside the recorder's client-side estimate so both figures read one number and are comparable when they disagree.

nodes.label: D90: SessionSpec gains budget_micros
nodes.rationale: TransportBuilder::build takes no run context, so the cap cannot arrive that way; SessionSpec is the per-session context and the field is additive for the fake and ACP.

nodes.label: F-10: --max-budget-usd 0 kills the turn
nodes.rationale: Zero is rejected before a byte is read, which would turn 'no cap' into 'no turn', so an absent or zero budget passes no flag.

nodes.label: D76: the default column shows the whole model id
nodes.community_name: D76: the default column shows the whole model id
nodes.norm_label: d76: the default column shows the whole model id
nodes.rationale: A truncated model id is not acceptable because the id is the coordinate ANA-4 §4.4 selects by — 'gemini-3.' names nothing. The eight columns cannot all be full at 98 usable columns, so the maintainer ranked the trade rather than leaving it to whoever renders last.

nodes.label: T47: the default column shows the whole model id
nodes.community_name: D76: the default column shows the whole model id
nodes.norm_label: t47: the default column shows the whole model id

nodes.label: T48: the packing correction — name donates
nodes.community_name: D76: the default column shows the whole model id
nodes.norm_label: t48: the packing correction — name donates
nodes.rationale: T47 paid for default's width from on this box, leaving it at 11 while its cells were 'unauthenticated' (15), which broke MOD-21's legible login. name held Length(12) for at most 'amp-acp' (7) — an allowance nothing used — so taking it to 8 returns exactly the four columns needed without changing any wording.

nodes.label: D21: Windows written and lint-checked from Linux, verified by MOD-16
nodes.community_name: D21: Windows written and lint-checked from Linux, verified by MOD-16
nodes.norm_label: d21: windows written and lint-checked from linux, verified by mod-16
nodes.rationale: This box has the x86_64-pc-windows-msvc target for clippy and nothing to run it on; listing the deferred facts by name is what lets MOD-16 pick them up instead of rediscovering them.

nodes.label: H-16: the Windows clippy detector is unavailable, not green
nodes.community_name: D21: Windows written and lint-checked from Linux, verified by MOD-16
nodes.norm_label: h-16: the windows clippy detector is unavailable, not green
nodes.rationale: clippy for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc dies in ring's build script ('failed to find tool lib.exe') before any htui code compiles, so the guard is unavailable; no Windows-specific code is added, so exposure is nil but 'green' would be a claim about a command that did not run.

nodes.label: D87: DriverFactory::with_acp becomes production
nodes.rationale: The name becomes false the moment cli/claude_stream_json is registered beside acp, and a constructor that lies about its contents is the trap adapter_ids exists to prevent.

nodes.label: D88: name-keyed seed top-up, not a migration
nodes.community_name: D88: name-keyed seed top-up, not a migration
nodes.norm_label: d88: name-keyed seed top-up, not a migration
nodes.rationale: seed_if_empty_as fires only on an empty table, so every box that has ever launched would never see claude-cli; a MOD-2 0003 migration is refused because 0003 is MOD-4's and the collision would be worse.

nodes.label: D89: Settings name column becomes the flexible one
nodes.community_name: D89: Settings name column becomes the flexible one
nodes.norm_label: d89: settings name column becomes the flexible one
nodes.rationale: A fixed Length(128) is arithmetically impossible — the eight columns share exactly 91 at the 98-column section and every other column sits at its own floor — so Min(10) makes the intent real rather than nominal, with on this box paying 2.

nodes.label: D15: open-question rulings (ReadStore conformance, prompt_digest)
nodes.rationale: Neither question has a consumer inside these milestones; both are recorded so M9's plan inherits a decision, not a question.

nodes.label: D16: deliberately absent from M1-M2
nodes.rationale: Scope discipline per the PRD; each omission is a named seam, not a plan.

nodes.label: D100: assembler scrubs by wrapping each section in Value::String
nodes.community_name: D100: assembler scrubs by wrapping each section in Value::String
nodes.norm_label: d100: assembler scrubs by wrapping each section in value::string
nodes.rationale: Wrapping is two lines and keeps R-SEC-3's single fail-closed implementation, which is what makes MOD-10's replacement 'behind an unchanged trait' still true; a scrub_text method would give MOD-10 two surfaces to replace. Scrubbing per section means Unmasked.path names the section, the fact a maintainer can act on.

nodes.label: D101: assemble() takes a fully resolved Budget
nodes.community_name: D101: assemble() takes a fully resolved Budget
nodes.norm_label: d101: assemble() takes a fully resolved budget
nodes.rationale: assemble() is pure by contract and a store read inside it would end that. The compiled-in DEFAULTS table is not a duplicate for its own sake: app_setting has no cache mirror and no generic reader, so an offline box has no other way to learn token_budget, and SEEDED_SETTINGS is typed [(&str, i32); 2] and cannot express prompt_reserve_fraction = 0.10.

nodes.label: D102: the preview is a sixth Backlog detail sub-tab
nodes.community_name: D102: the preview is a sixth Backlog detail sub-tab
nodes.norm_label: d102: the preview is a sixth backlog detail sub-tab
nodes.rationale: A sub-tab holds no store handle by rule (R-NF-3), so an assembly that reads five tables and walks a filesystem has to be deferred work off the UI task — milestone 5's ProbeAgents shape. Writing nothing is correctness, not caution: set_step_prompt writes a step's audit row and a preview has no step.

nodes.label: D103: preview stand-ins declared in trim_record.notes
nodes.community_name: D103: preview stand-ins declared in trim_record.notes
nodes.norm_label: d103: preview stand-ins declared in trim_record.notes
nodes.rationale: Inventing an input_kinds order or pointing the excerpt walk at the process's working directory would make the preview's bytes a thing no real run would produce, defeating its only purpose. notes is where ANA-5 puts conditions that are not errors, and the empty excerpt case proves criterion 12 rather than dodging it.

nodes.label: D104: ten default bodies ship as DEFAULT_TEMPLATES
nodes.community_name: D104: ten default bodies ship as DEFAULT_TEMPLATES
nodes.norm_label: d104: ten default bodies ship as default_templates
nodes.rationale: Confirming the bodies needs them in the tree, parsed and pinned by golden prompts (MOD-2's); seeding them into every project's prompt_template rows needs a project-creation path and is MOD-15's by name. A constant satisfies the first without pre-empting the second and gives MOD-15 something to seed from.

nodes.label: D105: skill model types land here, read-only
nodes.community_name: D105: skill model types land here, read-only
nodes.norm_label: d105: skill model types land here, read-only
nodes.rationale: ANA-5 §8 makes them a shared prerequisite of MOD-2 and MOD-9, whichever lands first owns them. The skills section is protected and its cap refuses the step, so criteria 10 and 15 cannot be tested without the types; the writers are MOD-9's, so a read-only model layer is the whole of what this milestone can honestly own.

nodes.label: D106: RunStepSummary gains prompt_tokens and trimmed
nodes.community_name: D106: RunStepSummary gains prompt_tokens and trimmed
nodes.norm_label: d106: runstepsummary gains prompt_tokens and trimmed
nodes.rationale: Two fields on a projection three backends compute is the cost; a third pane would be a fourth place the same record is formatted. Putting the table in the Prompt sub-tab means one view renders a preview's record and a stored step's record through one code path, which stops the two drifting.

nodes.label: D107: all three template roles implemented in the pure assembler
nodes.community_name: D107: all three template roles implemented in the pure assembler
nodes.norm_label: d107: all three template roles implemented in the pure assembler
nodes.rationale: The role-specific trim orders are inside trim.rs either way, so building only Phase would leave five SectionName variants unreachable that MOD-4 would re-derive. What MOD-2 cannot do is persist them: criterion 18 needs a handoff prompt written as a follow_up event, which needs a promotion, which is R-ORCH-5 and MOD-4's.

nodes.label: D95: PromptScope is the upstream_summaries argument
nodes.community_name: D95: PromptScope is the upstream_summaries argument
nodes.norm_label: d95: promptscope is the upstream_summaries argument
nodes.rationale: Scope::single_project would have to invent a workspace_id for the no-workspace case, and R-ENT-2 says there are no implicit workspace rows. Scope has 20+ sites across five crates all meaning 'the active workspace'; widening that meaning for one new method is how a shipped invariant erodes. The SQL takes $workspace and $project separately so the separate type costs nothing at the query.

nodes.label: D96: additive READ_CASES harness beside run_case
nodes.community_name: D96: additive READ_CASES harness beside run_case
nodes.norm_label: d96: additive read_cases harness beside run_case
nodes.rationale: run_case is already generic and its bound cannot be relaxed to ReadStore because eleven of twenty-two cases call write methods. A parallel READ_CASES list is additive, costs no existing case a byte, and follows milestone 8's D80: do not widen a shipped private API for one assertion.

nodes.label: D98: excerpt rendering is uniform across agent families
nodes.community_name: D98: excerpt rendering is uniform across agent families
nodes.norm_label: d98: excerpt rendering is uniform across agent families
nodes.rationale: An agent-dependent digest would break invariant 3's fan-out identity the moment MOD-4 mixed families across a fan-out; nothing measured in milestones 3–8 argues for divergence, and one rendering is one golden snapshot per fixture instead of two.

nodes.label: H-17: latch_quota awaits a store write inside record
nodes.community_name: H-17: latch_quota awaits a store write inside record
nodes.norm_label: h-17: latch_quota awaits a store write inside record
nodes.rationale: Accepted: the write is one indexed UPDATE and a usage row is rare; if it ever matters the latch moves to sync_step's cadence — same document, fewer writes.

nodes.label: D71: per-run cap enforced, per-batch cap deferred to MOD-12
nodes.community_name: D71: per-run cap enforced, per-batch cap deferred to MOD-12
nodes.norm_label: d71: per-run cap enforced, per-batch cap deferred to mod-12
nodes.rationale: ANA-4 §9 assigns the batch cap to MOD-12; a batch spans runs MOD-4 does not yet create, so enforcing it here would mean inventing the batch identity, which is R-ORCH territory.
